messages:
Maya: :rotating_light: paging: embeddings endpoint showing elevated 5xx errors for EU region (eu-central). Observed spike at ~08:22 UTC.
IncidentBot: New incident created INC-2026-0789. Auto-escalation to on-call.
Leo: oncall ack — seeing ~30% 503s for short embed ops, a subset of pods hitting OOM.
Priya: checking infra: `redwood infra pools describe embeddings-eu` -> pods Ready: 6/10, two in CrashLoopBackOff.
Maya: quick mitigation — remove eu routing from global LB for embeddings and route to eu-fallback (eu-3). I'll flip the policy in 60s.
Karen: do we have any Dedicated customers pinned to the primary cluster? If yes, they could be impacted.
Leo: pulling pin metadata now. `select customer_id, pinned_cluster from customers where pinned_cluster = 'eu-primary'` -> 3 dedicated accounts pinned.
Priya: starting scale action on eu-3: `redwood infra scale --pool embeddings-eu-fallback --replicas 14` and warming model v2.4.0.
Maya: filing quick status page update draft: "We're investigating elevated error rates for the embeddings API in the EU region. Traffic is being shifted to a fallback cluster and we have active mitigations underway. Next update in 15 minutes."
Support: Suggest adding: "Dedicated capacity pinned to eu-primary may be affected. If you are pinned, contact Support."
Maya: good call, include that.
IncidentBot: Status page draft created: https://staging.status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-0789/draft
Leo: logs show repeated oom_killer on node runtime-eu-41 around 08:19:
```
[08:19:12] runtime-eu-41 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2374 (runtime) score 1200
[08:19:13] runtime-eu-41 runtime: evicting KV cache shard 12
[08:20:01] gateway: upstream returned 503 for /v1/embeddings
```
Priya: looks like KV cache reclaim under large-seq loads. Could be the batching change rolled two days ago.
Leo: propose rollback of batching change on eu-primary canary node first.
Maya: agree. Initiating canary rollback. DeployBot: rollback job queued (job-9002).
IncidentBot: Deploy job-9002 started.
Karen: parallel task — BillingOps, we'll need to start calculating potential SLA credits. Criteria: any Dedicated customer pinned to eu-primary for any duration of the incident window, plus any multi-tenant customer with >1% error rate during window.
BillingOps: acknowledged. Which time window should we use?
Maya: let's capture the window from first observed anomaly 08:18 to mitigation baseline 08:50 (time we restore routing).
BillingOps: noted. I'll export per-customer error counts and request volumes for that window. Command I'll run: `redwood metrics query --from 1798765100 --to 1798767400 --metric errors.rate --group customer_id --filter endpoint=embeddings > /tmp/emb-sla-window.csv`
Support: drafting customer notification template for impacted accounts (short, non-alarmist):
"Hi <Customer>,

We detected elevated error rates affecting the embeddings API in the EU region between 08:18 and 08:50 UTC. Traffic was shifted to a fallback cluster and we applied mitigations; service has been restored. Our billing team is evaluating eligibility for SLA credits for impacted customers and will follow up within 48 hours. If you experienced issues, please reply to this message or open a support ticket.

— Redwood Support"

Maya: add line about next steps for Dedicated customers: how to request manual failover or pin changes if they want extra protection.
Priya: can we also include a quick recommended retry/backoff pattern to customers? e.g., exponential backoff with max 3 retries and jitter.
Support: will include that in the targeted outreach.
DeployBot: rollback job-9002 completed on canary at 08:33 — canary metrics show error rate dropped to 0.6%.
Leo: canary looks good. Starting phased reintroduction of 10% traffic to eu-primary at 08:40. Monitoring.
Maya: good. Keep the phased plan: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with 5m observation windows.
Leo: region-wide error rate down to 1.8% after partial reintro.
Maya: set target for full recovery: error rate <1% for 10m before marking restored.
Priya: eu-fallback scaled and ready: `redwood infra status --pool embeddings-eu-fallback` -> replicas 14, ready 14.
BillingOps: exported CSV and running assessment. Quick note on policy: we offer a pro-rata credit for the affected minutes where SLA thresholds were missed. For dedicated customers, we check pinning metadata and committed throughput windows. For multi-tenant customers, threshold is error rate >1% during any 30-minute sliding window.
BillingOps: preliminary result — 3 dedicated accounts pinned to eu-primary during window; 9 multi-tenant customers surpass 1% error rate in window. Gathering volumes to compute credit amounts.
Maya: good. Please preserve the raw metrics in /incidents/INC-2026-0789/artifacts for audit.
BillingOps: will upload CSV and calculation sheet. Also will coordinate language with Legal if we need specific contractual phrasing.
Support: preparing targeted DM for the 12 flagged customers — will hold until BillingOps confirms eligibility list.
Karen: ops note — create an action item to revert batching change in the EU release branch until we have root cause confirmed.
Maya: agree. Also schedule a load test with synthetic large-seq traffic to validate fix.
IncidentBot: Update posted to status page at 08:46: mitigation underway, partial recovery observed.
Leo: final check — region error rate 0.9%, p95 latency near baseline. Moving incident to mitigated status.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-0789 status updated: mitigated at 08:55 UTC.
BillingOps: final eligibility list: 3 Dedicated (IDs redacted) and 9 multi-tenant accounts. Computing credits now; expect to send Support final list and templated customer emails within 24h.
Support: drafting SLA-credit offer template for eligible customers (include timeline):
"Hi <Customer>,

Thanks for your patience. Following INC-2026-0789, our review indicates your service experienced elevated error rates for the embeddings API in the EU region between 08:18 and 08:50 UTC. Based on our SLA policy, you are eligible for a pro-rated credit which will be applied to your next invoice within 30 days. If you prefer a dedicated review or have questions about the calculation, reply to this thread and we will prioritize your case.

— Redwood Billing & Support"

Maya: approve. Action items:
- BillingOps: upload calculation + handoff to Support (due 24h)
- Priya: confirm autoscaling thresholds and warm-pool sizes (due EOD)
- Leo: include sample offending request patterns (seq_len distribution) in postmortem (due EOD)
- Support: prepare targeted outbound messages but do not send until BillingOps confirms list (hold)
Maya: linking to postmortem ticket INC-2026-0789-POST and closing active mitigation channel. Great job, team. :thumbsup:
